---
title: "Applying the model"
subtitle: "Accessing the SDD ensembles and estimating Secchi disc depth for new Landsat observations"
---

This page describes how to obtain the SDD ensembles and apply them to new data with the helper functions in the source repository. Two models are published, and the same helpers apply both:

| Model | Inputs | Model card |
|---|---|---|
| Production | Landsat bands and indices, catchment characteristics, shoreline flag, antecedent weather | [Production](model_card.qmd) |
| Band-only | Landsat bands and indices only | [Band-only](model_card_band_only.qmd) |

The model cards cover what each model is, how it performs, how the two compare, and where they should not be used; read the card for the model you use before applying it. [Step 07](regional_clarity/07_regional_application.Rmd) (production) and [step 07b](regional_clarity/07b_regional_application_band_only.Rmd) (band-only) are complete worked applications across the region that use the same functions described here.

Applying the model takes four steps:

1. **Obtain QA'd Landsat observations** at your sites, harmonized to Landsat 7 (R, `AquaMatchr`).
2. **Prepare model inputs**: spectral indices, plus site characteristics, antecedent weather, and feature coarsening for the production model (R, `prepare_model_inputs.R`).
3. **Predict SDD** with the 40-member ensemble (Python `apply_model.py`, or R).
4. **Screen the estimates** with the applicability checks (Python `apply_model.py`, or R).

Steps 1 and 2 run in R because they share their code with the training pipeline. Building inputs with the same functions that built the training data guarantees that a feature means the same thing at application time as it did in training. Steps 3 and 4 need only the model folder, so they run without the training data.

## Accessing the models

Each model is published on the Hugging Face Hub, and the same folders are tracked in the source repository:

| Model | Hugging Face Hub | Repository folder |
|---|---|---|
| Production | [`bgsteele/intermountain-west-regional-clarity-sdd-landsat`](https://huggingface.co/bgsteele/intermountain-west-regional-clarity-sdd-landsat) | [`regional_clarity/xg_models/v3_production/`](https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model/tree/main/regional_clarity/xg_models/v3_production) |
| Band-only | [`bgsteele/intermountain-west-regional-clarity-sdd-landsat-band-only`](https://huggingface.co/bgsteele/intermountain-west-regional-clarity-sdd-landsat-band-only) | [`regional_clarity/xg_models/v3_band_only/`](https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model/tree/main/regional_clarity/xg_models/v3_band_only) |

Either copy works with the helper functions; pass its path as `model_dir`. The examples below use the production model; for the band-only model, substitute its repository ID or folder.

The Hub copy holds only model artifacts. The helper code lives in the source repository, so clone the repository in either case:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model.git
```

To download the model from the Hub instead of using the repository copy:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

model_dir = snapshot_download("bgsteele/intermountain-west-regional-clarity-sdd-landsat")
```

or, from the command line, `hf download bgsteele/intermountain-west-regional-clarity-sdd-landsat --local-dir v3_production`.

### What a model folder contains

Both model folders have the same layout:

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `seed601/` … `seed610/` | One folder per ensemble seed. |
| `seed*/xgboost_fold{1-4}.json` | The four fitted boosters for that seed, in XGBoost JSON format. Each contains only the trees up to its early-stopping iteration. |
| `seed*/backward_elim_summary.json` | That seed's selected features, in model order, under `final_features`. |
| `seed*/final_tune_xgboost.json` | That seed's tuned hyperparameters (also lists `features`). |
| `seed*/final_eval_summary.json` | That seed's CV and holdout metrics. |
| `ensemble_mean_abs_shap.csv` | Ensemble mean \|SHAP\| per feature; also the weights for the AOA check. |
| `supplemental_feature_table.csv` | Every candidate feature, its pruning outcome, and which seeds kept it. |
| `applicability/aoa_parameters.json` | AOA threshold and scaling, the training range of every model input, the seasonal window, training missions, and the minimum training SDD. |
| `applicability/aoa_reference.csv` | The training observations in AOA space, for the nearest-neighbor dissimilarity index. |

Each of the 40 boosters is fit on its own seed's feature set, so seeds differ in which inputs they use. The full input set is the union across seeds, listed in each model card's Features table ([production](model_card.qmd#features), [band-only](model_card_band_only.qmd#features)). Every row you predict on needs every input in that union.

## Environment setup

**R** (steps 1–2, and optionally 3–4): `tidyverse`, `sf`, `arrow`, `elevatr`, `StreamCatTools`, `climateR`, `data.table`, and `parallel`; plus [`AquaMatchr`](https://github.com/AquaSat/AquaMatchr) (`remotes::install_github("AquaSat/AquaMatchr")`) for data access. `prepare_model_inputs.R` loads all of these when sourced, so they must be installed even when preparing band-only inputs. Predicting and screening in R also needs `xgboost`, `jsonlite`, and `RANN`.

**Python** (steps 3–4): build the environment described in the repository README's [Python environment](https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model#python-environment) section from `requirements-lock.txt`. `apply_model.py` itself needs only `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, and `xgboost`; the environment also includes `huggingface_hub` for downloading the model from the Hub.

::: {.callout-warning}
## macOS: set the OpenMP variables first
Export `KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE` and `OMP_NUM_THREADS` (e.g. 4) **before** importing XGBoost. Without them, XGBoost can load a competing OpenMP runtime and oversubscribe the CPU.
:::

## Step 1: Obtain QA'd Landsat observations

The model was trained on [AquaMatch siteSR](https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/f85622d6d32ef7fe6cff8d63c3b947c9) data: Landsat Collection 2 surface reflectance and temperature summarized at water-quality monitoring sites, harmonized across missions to Landsat 7. New observations have to come from the same product and pass the same QA, otherwise the reflectance values are not comparable to the training data. [Step 00](regional_clarity/00_download_AquaMatch_data.Rmd) downloads and harmonizes the data with `AquaMatchr`:

```r
library(AquaMatchr)   # requires an EDI account; set EDI_API_key in .Renviron

download_siteSR(download_folder = data_dir, version = "newest", algal_mask = FALSE)
build_sr(which_sr = "siteSR", sr_location = data_dir, algal_mask = FALSE,
         output_file = file.path(data_dir, "siteSR_DSWE1_full_concatenation.parquet"))
apply_handoffs(input_path = file.path(data_dir, "siteSR_DSWE1_full_concatenation.parquet"),
               handoff_path = list.files(data_dir, pattern = "handoff", full.names = TRUE),
               correction_method = "Gardner_poly", sat_target = "LS7", algal_mask = FALSE,
               output_file = file.path(data_dir, "siteSR_DSWE1_LS7corr.parquet"))
download_sceneMetadata(download_folder = data_dir, product = "siteSR")
```

The handoffs must target Landsat 7 (`sat_target = "LS7"`); the `*_corr_7` bands are what the model was trained on.

[Step 01](regional_clarity/01_filter_AquaMatch_Data.Rmd)'s "Remote Sensing Filters" section is the reference implementation of the observation QA. It covers:

- **Site geometry.** Keep sites whose buffer intersects exactly one waterbody (`number_int_wb == 1`) on an NHDPlusV2 waterbody (`wb_nhd_source == "NHDPlusv2"`).
- **Pixel quality.** Keep rows with `pCount_dswe1 / pCount_dswe_gt0 > 0.5`, `pCount_dswe1 > 8`, and `prop_clouds == 0`.
- **Scene quality.** Keep scenes with `CLOUD_COVER < 20` in the scene metadata (joined on `sat_id`).
- **Band outliers.** Remove per-site reflectance outliers with the multiband RANSAC filter (`ransac_site_multiband()`).

This QA is check 1 of the model card's [applicability checks](model_card.qmd#applicability-checks). It cannot be applied after prediction, so it has to be done here.

The output of this step is two tables that the next step takes as input:

| Table | One row per | Required columns |
|---|---|---|
| `sites` | site | `siteSR_id`, `WGS84_Latitude`, `WGS84_Longitude`, `wb_nhd_id` (NHDPlusV2 COMID), `wb_nhd_source`, `flag_wb`, `flag_optical_shoreline` |
| `sitesr_rows` | QA-passing observation | `siteSR_id`, `date`, `mission`, `red_corr_7`, `green_corr_7`, `blue_corr_7`, `nir_corr_7`, `swir1_corr_7`, `swir2_corr_7`, `surfacetemp_corr_7` |

`sites` comes straight from AquaMatch's siteSR site table (`siteSR_collated_WQP_NWIS_sites_with_NHD_info_*.csv`), and `sitesr_rows` from the QA'd siteSR parquet.

::: {.callout-note}
## Locations not in siteSR
siteSR covers Water Quality Portal and NWIS monitoring sites. For other locations, the [siteSR pipeline](https://github.com/AquaSat/AquaMatch_siteSR) can be adapted to extract surface reflectance at a custom set of points, producing data that matches the product the model was trained on. We are also developing a standalone method for custom-location extraction.
:::

## Step 2: Prepare model inputs (R)

[`regional_clarity/R/prepare_model_inputs.R`](https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model/blob/main/regional_clarity/R/prepare_model_inputs.R) turns those two tables into one model-ready row per observation. For most uses, one call does everything:

```r
source("regional_clarity/R/prepare_model_inputs.R")

model_input <- prepare_model_inputs(sites, sitesr_rows)
arrow::write_parquet(model_input, "model_input.parquet")
```

For the production model, `prepare_model_inputs()` fetches elevation (AWS terrain tiles via `elevatr`), LakeCat catchment metrics (EPA StreamCat via `StreamCatTools`), and daily gridMET weather (via `climateR`). It then summarizes antecedent weather, computes spectral indices, coarsens the site features, and joins everything. It needs network access, and the gridMET fetch is the slow part. Its arguments:

- `keep` names extra `sitesr_rows` columns to carry through to the output (for example, your own identifiers).
- `n_workers` sets the number of parallel gridMET requests (default 8).
- `site_and_weather = FALSE` prepares inputs for the band-only model. Nothing is fetched, and the output holds only the bands, LaSRC flag, and spectral indices. Of the `sites` table, only `siteSR_id` is used.

```r
model_input <- prepare_model_inputs(sites, sitesr_rows, site_and_weather = FALSE)
```

Cells that fail to fetch after one retry produce a warning, and their rows are left with missing weather. Those rows then fail the completeness check in step 4.

### Function reference

The individual steps are exposed as functions so you can cache intermediate results or reuse values you already have. [Step 07](regional_clarity/07_regional_application.Rmd) calls them separately, caching each fetch.

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `prepare_model_inputs(sites, sitesr_rows, keep, n_workers, site_and_weather)` | Runs all of the steps below, or only `assemble_model_inputs()` with `site_and_weather = FALSE`. |
| `fetch_site_characteristics(sites, existing = NULL)` | Elevation, LakeCat catchment area and 2006 land cover, and `shore_flag` per site. Rows of `existing` (same columns) are reused and only the remaining sites are fetched. Stops if any site's waterbody is not from NHDPlusV2. |
| `gridmet_cells(sites)` | The 1/24° gridMET cell each site falls in. Sites sharing a cell share weather. |
| `gridmet_cell_ranges(sitesr_rows, site_cells)` | The date range each cell needs: its observation dates plus the 30-day antecedent window. |
| `fetch_gridmet(cell_ranges, n_workers)` | Daily precipitation, maximum and minimum temperature, and solar radiation per cell, fetched in parallel. Returns `list(weather, failed)`. |
| `summarize_weather(weather_raw)` | 1-, 3-, 7- and 30-day summaries per cell and date. Each window covers the days strictly *before* the image date. |
| `add_features(df)` | Spectral ratios and indices, plus coarsening of whichever catchment and land-cover features are present. |
| `assemble_model_inputs(sitesr_rows, site_char, site_cells, weather_summaries, keep)` | Renames the bands to model names, sets `atm_corr_LaSRC`, joins site characteristics and weather, and calls `add_features()`. Leave `site_char`, or `site_cells` and `weather_summaries`, as `NULL` to skip those joins. |

`add_features()` applies the same feature engineering as the training pipeline, including the fixed catchment-area cap (`CATCHMENT_WINSORIZE_CAP_SQKM`, 617.1 km²). The cap is the training-data 99th percentile and must not be recomputed from new data.

### Building inputs in Python instead

If you assemble site characteristics and weather yourself, [`regional_clarity/python/features.py`](https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model/blob/main/regional_clarity/python/features.py) provides the Python originals of the last step: `add_spectral_indices()` and `coarsen_site_features()`. Every other input has to match the definitions in `prepare_model_inputs.R` exactly: column names, units, the NLCD 2006 vintage, the window definitions, and the `shore_flag` rule. Using the R functions is the safer path.

## Step 3: Predict SDD

[`regional_clarity/python/apply_model.py`](https://github.com/rossyndicate/regional-clarity-RS-model/blob/main/regional_clarity/python/apply_model.py) loads the ensemble and predicts:

```python
import sys

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, "regional_clarity/python")
from apply_model import load_ensemble, predict_sdd

model_dir = "regional_clarity/xg_models/v3_production"   # or v3_band_only, or a snapshot_download() path
X = pd.read_parquet("model_input.parquet")

members = load_ensemble(model_dir)          # 40 (features, booster) pairs
X["pred_sdd"] = predict_sdd(members, X)     # ensemble mean, in metres
```

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `load_ensemble(model_dir)` | Returns the 40 members (10 seeds × 4 folds) as `(features, booster)` pairs, with each seed's feature list read from its `backward_elim_summary.json`. |
| `predict_sdd(members, X)` | Gives each booster its own seed's features, in order, and returns the mean of the 40 predictions. `X` may carry extra columns. |

Applied to the training repository's holdout, this reproduces each model's published holdout RMSE: 1.2567 m for production and 1.3558 m for band-only (scored once per unique site and date).

### Predicting in R

To stay in R, load each seed's features and boosters and average. This is the prediction step in steps [07](regional_clarity/07_regional_application.Rmd) and [07b](regional_clarity/07b_regional_application_band_only.Rmd), and it gives the same predictions:

```r
library(xgboost)
library(jsonlite)

model_dir <- "regional_clarity/xg_models/v3_production"

seed_preds <- sapply(601:610, \(s) {
  seed_dir <- file.path(model_dir, paste0("seed", s))
  feats <- fromJSON(file.path(seed_dir, "backward_elim_summary.json"))$final_features
  X <- as.matrix(model_input[, feats])
  rowMeans(sapply(1:4, \(fold) predict(xgb.load(file.path(seed_dir, paste0("xgboost_fold", fold, ".json"))), X)))
})
model_input$pred_sdd <- rowMeans(seed_preds)
model_input$pred_seed_sd <- apply(seed_preds, 1, sd)
```

The spread across seeds (`pred_seed_sd`, typically about 0.12 m for production and 0.09 m for band-only) measures how much the ensemble members disagree. It is not a prediction interval: typical error against in situ SDD is about 1.3 m for production and 1.4 m for band-only.

## Step 4: Screen the estimates

Use an estimate only if it passes every applicability check. `check_applicability()` runs checks 2–7 from the model card ([production](model_card.qmd#applicability-checks), [band-only](model_card_band_only.qmd#applicability-checks)) using only the model folder's `applicability/` files:

```python
from apply_model import check_applicability

flags = check_applicability(X, model_dir, pred_sdd=X["pred_sdd"])
X = X.join(flags)
usable = X[X["pass_all"]]
```

Always pass the same `model_dir` you predicted with. Each model's training ranges, AOA features, and DI threshold are its own, so screening one model's estimates with the other's files gives wrong results.

`X` needs `date` and `mission` columns (`LT04`, `LT05`, `LE07`, `LC08`, or `LC09`) in addition to the model inputs; `prepare_model_inputs()` carries both through. The checks are cumulative, so each `pass_*` column is true only if the row also passed every earlier check:

| Column | Check |
|---|---|
| `pass_mission` | Landsat mission represented in training. |
| `pass_season` | Day of year within the training window (70–320). |
| `pass_complete` | Every model input is present. |
| `pass_range` | Every model input falls within its training range. |
| `di` | Dissimilarity index: weighted, standardized distance to the nearest training observation (Meyer & Pebesma 2021). Missing when an AOA feature is missing. |
| `pass_aoa` | Inside the area of applicability (`di` at or below the threshold in `aoa_parameters.json`). |
| `pass_plausible` | Prediction no shallower than the training minimum (0.1 m). Only present when `pred_sdd` is given. |
| `pass_all` | Passed every check. |

Without `pred_sdd`, `pass_all` stops at the AOA check, so you can screen observations before predicting. The per-check columns show *why* a row failed, which is often worth reporting: for example, a waterbody that falls outside the AOA on every date is beyond what the model has learned, while scattered seasonal failures are not.

For an R implementation of the same checks, see the "Applicability checks" section of [step 07](regional_clarity/07_regional_application.Rmd) or [step 07b](regional_clarity/07b_regional_application_band_only.Rmd). The Python and R versions give identical results.

## Before you use the estimates

- **Check the limitations.** Both models compress clear-water estimates above about 6 m SDD and overestimate below about 2 m. Read the Limitations section of the model card ([production](model_card.qmd#limitations), [band-only](model_card_band_only.qmd#limitations)) before interpreting trends or extremes.
- **Stay inside the training region.** The models were trained on six states of the intermountain West (CO, ID, MT, NM, UT, WY). The applicability checks catch observations that look unlike the training data, but they do not establish that either model transfers to a different region.
- **Use the same data product.** Reflectance from a different atmospheric correction, harmonization reference, or extraction method is not interchangeable with siteSR's `*_corr_7` bands, even when the column names match.
- **Report the version.** Cite the model as described in [How to cite](index.qmd#how-to-cite), including the release you used and which model (production or band-only) produced the estimates.
